questions.q: In the target-state architecture, what are the four source systems feeding Summit?
options: Atlas, Beacon, Comet, and Harbor
Snowflake, Purview, Power BI, and Summit
Only Atlas and Beacon
Dana Whitfield's executive dashboards
questions.explain: The lesson's diagram shows Atlas, Beacon, Comet, and Harbor as the four source systems flowing into Summit through ELT jobs.

questions.q: What has to happen before data moves from the raw zone into the conformed zone?
options: Nothing — all data moves automatically with no checks
Lesson 7's data quality gate must be applied, per CDE
The data must first be deleted and re-entered manually
It must be approved by the board
questions.explain: The architecture diagram places Lesson 7's quality gate between the raw zone and the conformed zone, applied per CDE.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say Snowflake-plus-Purview-plus-Power BI fits LTV Global specifically, rather than being a generic recommendation?
options: Because it is the cheapest option available on the market
Atlas is already SQL Server, reporting is already Power BI, three of four sources are already cloud SaaS, and Purview enforces metadata on the real tables rather than a separate drifting document
Because Dana Whitfield personally prefers Snowflake
Because no other platform exists
questions.explain: The lesson gives three specific reasons tied to LTV Global's existing stack and source locations, not a generic best-practice claim.

questions.q: Who owns the golden zone (the Customer golden record) in the architecture's ownership mapping?
options: No one — it is unowned and unreviewed
Only Dana Whitfield, with no one else involved
It is jointly owned by the relevant domain owners, reviewed at the monthly Data Governance Council
Only the IT & Data Services representative
questions.explain: The lesson states the golden zone is jointly owned per Lesson 9's decision and reviewed at the monthly council, unlike the single-owner raw and conformed zones.

questions.q: How do Lesson 13's two AI pilots connect to this architecture?
options: The support assistant reads directly from raw Beacon and Comet tables with no governance
They are not part of the architecture at all
Both models read from governed zones — forecasting from the post-quality-gate conformed zone, and the support assistant from a scrubbed, governed extract rather than raw tables
They replace Power BI as the only consumption layer
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says both AI pilots are consumption-layer citizens reading from governed zones, with no side door around the architecture.
